summary: Adds a new 78-line research note arguing that a good adversarial review of an AI chatbot rests on discipline, not clever jailbreaks: explicit impact-first threat model, diverse and partly independent testers, taxonomy-anchored reproducible methodology, manual plus automated probing, severity grading, and a closed remediate-retest loop. It surveys NIST, OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind, and Feffer et al., lists pitfalls of weak reviews, gives a four-stage recommendation, and closes with caveats about field immaturity and vendor-sourced figures.

claims.text: Feffer et al. (AIES 2024) found red-teaming purpose is often vague and warned of security theater without structure.
NIST AI 600-1 defines 12 GenAI risk categories and places red teaming under Measure as recurring.
OpenAI external red teaming white paper is arXiv 2503.16431 (Ahmad, Agarwal, Lampe, Mishkin, 2025) with four design steps.
Crescendomation achieves 29-61% higher performance on GPT-4, 49-71% on Gemini-Pro, 98% binary success (arXiv:2404.01833).
Constitutional Classifiers cut jailbreak success 86% to 4.4% at 23.7% compute increase, 0.38% refusal rise.
Constitutional Classifiers++ released January 9, 2026 at ~1% additional compute with no universal jailbreak found.

risks.note: Bug-bounty participant counts (405 of ~800, 339, 300,000 interactions, 8 levels) have no source link.
Crescendo performance ranges quoted verbatim but chunk cannot confirm they match the arXiv paper.
Anthropic CVSS-modeled jailbreak scoring framework and a 2026 ASR-validity paper are named without citation.
OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026) and ASI Top 10 dated without a source.

least_confident: I could not check whether the many specific dates, arXiv ids, and percentages (especially the 2026-dated items the caveats flag) are accurate, since the chunk cites no verifiable links.
